nodes.text: Then, in the sight of the man of God, it was decided that they should dig the ground in that same place. As they went deeper by digging, the brothers found a bronze idol there. When this had been thrown for the moment, as it happened, into the kitchen, fire was suddenly seen to come out, and it appeared to the eyes of all the monks that the whole building of the kitchen was being consumed. And as they made a great noise throwing water and, as it were, putting out the fire, the man of God, roused by the same uproar, came. Perceiving that this fire was in the eyes of the brothers but not in his own, he at once bowed his head in prayer; and the brothers, whom he found deluded by a phantom fire, he called back [to themselves], and warned them to sign their eyes, so that they might both see that kitchen building standing unharmed and not see the flames which the ancient enemy had feigned.

But let me now return to the things I learned from the account of his disciples, named at the beginning of this book. A certain man was suffering from the most bitter rivalry of an adversary, whose hatred broke out to such a point that he gave him poison in a drink without his knowing. Though this could not take his life, it nevertheless changed the colour of his skin, so that a mottling spread over his body seemed to imitate the appearance of leprosy. But brought to the man of God, he quickly recovered his former health: for as soon as [Benedict] touched him, he drove away all the mottling of his skin.
